title: The Spiral Staircase
basedOn: Loosely inspired by the Michael Peterson case
summary: Renowned architect Arthur Pendelton called emergency services at two in the morning, reporting his wife Clara had fallen down the back stairs of their estate. Paramedics found a scene resembling a slaughterhouse, with Clara deceased from massive head trauma. The prosecution alleges Arthur bludgeoned her with a heavy fireplace poker that went missing that night. The defense maintains it was a catastrophic accidental fall after Clara consumed alcohol and prescription sedatives.
prosecutionStatement: Twenty-eight deep lacerations cover the back of the head of Clara Pendelton. A flat wooden staircase does not inflict that kind of targeted and repeated trauma. A solid brass fireplace poker does. Arthur wants you to believe his wife tripped and bled to death while he sat obliviously by the pool at two in the morning. He forgot to explain why the blood on the walls was already dry when paramedics arrived. You will see the cast-off spatter patterns that only come from a swinging weapon. This was not a tragic accident. This was a brutal and calculated execution.
defenseStatement: The entire case of the State rests on a phantom weapon that no one has ever seen. They have no motive, no witnesses, and absolutely no physical weapon. Clara mixed vodka with a heavy dose of Valium that night, leaving her dizzy and disoriented. She fell backward, striking her head on the sharp stone edge of the stair landing, trying to stand, and thrashing in a panic. The prosecution calls that a beating. A calculated execution requires intent, but Arthur was outside, completely unaware of the nightmare unfolding indoors. He lost the love of his life. Do not compound this catastrophe by condemning an innocent man to cover up an overzealous investigation.

evidence.title: Blood Spatter Analysis
evidence.description: Forensic report detailing cast-off patterns on the stairwell walls, indicating multiple overhead swings with a blunt object.

evidence.title: Toxicology Screen
evidence.description: Medical examiner report showing high levels of alcohol and prescription sedatives in the bloodstream of the victim at the time of death.

evidence.title: Paramedic Assessment
evidence.description: First responder documentation noting that the blood pooling around the head of the victim had already begun to coagulate and dry when they arrived.

evidence.title: Biomechanical Fall Simulation
evidence.description: Defense expert analysis demonstrating that the custom stone steps had unusually sharp edges capable of causing severe lacerations during a tumbling fall.

evidence.title: Joint Life Insurance Document
evidence.description: A life insurance policy paying out a substantial sum to the surviving spouse, established ten years prior and remaining untouched since.

evidence.title: Emergency Call Recording
evidence.description: Audio of the call for help from Arthur, featuring heavy breathing and confused, overlapping sentences.

evidence.title: Estate Security Logs
evidence.description: Alarm system records indicating no exterior doors were opened or closed between midnight and the arrival of first responders.
